sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Primary Sector (Agriculture & Allied)**: Involves the extraction and harvesting of natural products directly from the earth, including agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining.
• **Secondary Sector (Manufacturing & Industry)**: Involves the transformation of raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods through manufacturing, electricity, gas, water supply, and construction.
• **Tertiary Sector (Services)**: Involves the provision of intangible services that support primary and secondary sectors, as well as final consumers, including trade, transport, IT, banking, and real estate.
• **Quaternary & Quinary Extensions**: Sub-sectors of knowledge-based intellectual activities (R&D, education) and top-level decision-making (CEO, policymakers) respectively.

items.definition: Organized sector enterprises have fixed terms of employment, legal compliance, and social security benefits. Unorganized sector lacks formal contracts, job security, and regulatory oversight, dominating Indian labor markets (>80%).

Public sector enterprises (PSEs) are owned and managed by the government to fulfill social objectives and strategic industrialization. Private sector is driven by profit maximization and market efficiency.
Originally conceptualized by Fisher, Clark, and Fourastié, tracking economic evolution as shifts from agriculture to industry, and finally to services.
National Manufacturing Policy, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes, Code on Wages 2019, and Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) by NSO.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Primary Belts**: Indo-Gangetic plains (agriculture), Chota Nagpur Plateau (mineral extraction and mining hubs).
• **Industrial Corridors**: Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC), Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC) driving secondary manufacturing.
• **Service Hubs**: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Gurugram, and Chennai acting as global IT and financial capitals.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Structural rigidities, low female labor force participation (FLFP) in manufacturing, informalization of services (gig economy challenges).
• **Policy Interventions**: National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP), PM GatiShakti for logistics integration, formalization via e-Shram portal and GST.

items.title: Mnemonic for Classic 3-Sector Progression
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "P S T - People Smell Trouble" (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary)
• **Decoded Meaning**: Primary (Extraction) -> Secondary (Processing) -> Tertiary (Services).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls the chronological and developmental hierarchy of economic activities.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: India's structural paradox: Primary sector employs ~45% of workforce but contributes only ~18% to GVA; Tertiary sector employs ~30% but contributes >50% to GVA.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'The service sector employs the maximum share of India's workforce.' This is INCORRECT. While the service sector contributes the highest share to India's GVA, the primary (agriculture) sector still employs the largest share of the workforce.

Mains Value Addition: Quote the 'Kuznets Curve' regarding structural transformation (shift from agriculture to industry/services) and highlight India's unique 'Service-Led Growth' bypass of the traditional manufacturing stage.

keyTakeaways: Economic sectors classify activities into Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary based on value addition and nature of output.
India exhibits a unique structural anomaly: high GVA contribution from services alongside high employment retention in agriculture.
Distinguishing between organized/unorganized and public/private sectors is vital for analyzing labor welfare and macro-policies.
